A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=b""):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    for k in list(e):
        if k.startswith("BAT_"): del e[k]
    # env TERM?
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p
files={
 "py": b"import os\n# comment\nx = 1 + 'hi'\nprint(x)\n",
 "rs": b"fn main() { let x = 1; println!(\"{}\", x); } // hi\n",
 "js": b"const x = 1; // hi\nconsole.log('a');\n",
 "txt": b"hello world\n",
 "md": b"# Title\n\n**bold** text\n",
 "json": b'{"a": 1, "b": [true, null]}\n',
 "sh": b"#!/bin/bash\necho hi # comment\n",
}
for ext,dat in files.items():
    open(f"/tmp/t/x.{ext}","wb").write(dat)
    p=run(["--color=always","--paging=never","--style=plain","--decorations=never",f"/tmp/t/x.{ext}"])
    print(ext, repr(p.stdout))
print("--- themes py")
for theme in ["ansi","base16","base16-256","TwoDark","Monokai Extended","Solarized (dark)","Solarized (light)","GitHub","Dracula"]:
    p=run(["--color=always","--paging=never","--style=plain","--theme="+theme,"/tmp/t/x.py"])
    print(theme, repr(p.stdout[:500]))

p=pathlib.Path('src/highlight.py');s=p.read_text()
start=s.index('def highlight_man(text,hl):')
end=s.index('\ndef highlight_markdown')
new=r'''def highlight_man(text,hl):
    # collapse overstrike sequences X\bX / _\bX
    out=[]; i=0
    while i < len(text):
        if i+2 < len(text) and text[i+1]=='\b':
            out.append(text[i+2]); i+=3
        elif text[i]=='\b':
            i+=1
        else:
            out.append(text[i]); i+=1
    text=''.join(out)
    idx=getattr(hl,'_man_idx',0); hl._man_idx=idx+1
    if not text:
        return []
    if idx==0:
        # title line: try FOO(1)  Title  FOO(1)
        m=re.match(r'^(\S+)\(([^)]+)\)(\s+)(.*?)(\s+)(\S+)\(([^)]+)\)\s*$',text)
        if m:
            toks=[]
            toks.append(('help_command',m.group(1))); toks.append(('operator','(')); toks.append(('string',m.group(2))); toks.append(('operator',')')); toks.append(('default',m.group(3)))
            # middle words/spaces as heading tokens individual words + spaces
            for part in re.split(r'(\s+)',m.group(4)):
                if part: toks.append(('heading',part))
            toks.append(('default',m.group(5))); toks.append(('help_command',m.group(6))); toks.append(('operator','(')); toks.append(('string',m.group(7))); toks.append(('operator',')'))
            return toks
        return [('default',text)]
    if text[0] not in (' ','\t'):
        return [('heading',text)]
    return [('default',text)]

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
p.write_text(s)

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('src/app.py');s=p.read_text()
start=s.index('def colorize_clap_error(text):')
end=s.index("\nif __name__=='__main__':")
new=r'''def colorize_clap_error(text):
    prog=os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv and sys.argv[0] else 'bat'
    def Y(x): return f"\x1b[33m{x}\x1b[0m"
    def G(x): return f"\x1b[32m{x}\x1b[0m"
    def B(x): return f"\x1b[1m{x}\x1b[0m"
    lines=text.split('\n')
    out=[]
    for idx,line in enumerate(lines):
        if idx==0 and line.startswith('error:'):
            line='\x1b[1m\x1b[31merror:\x1b[0m'+line[len('error:'):]
            # quoted args coloring based on pattern
            m=re.search(r"(invalid value|unexpected value) '([^']*)' for '([^']*)'",line)
            if m:
                # replace from end to preserve indices
                line=line[:m.start(3)]+B(m.group(3))+line[m.end(3):]
                line=line[:m.start(2)]+Y(m.group(2))+line[m.end(2):]
            else:
                m=re.search(r"a value is required for '([^']*)'",line)
                if m:
                    line=line[:m.start(1)]+Y(m.group(1))+line[m.end(1):]
                else:
                    # color all quoted tokens on first line yellow (unknown / conflicts / multiple)
                    line=re.sub(r"'([^']*)'",lambda mm:"'"+Y(mm.group(1))+"'",line)
            out.append(line); continue
        if line.startswith('  tip:'):
            line=line.replace('tip:',G('tip:'),1)
            # quoted segments
            parts=re.split(r"('[^']*')",line)
            # first quoted after "to pass" yellow, others green; similar argument quoted green
            qcount=0
            for pi,part in enumerate(parts):
                if len(part)>=2 and part[0]=="'" and part[-1]=="'":
                    inner=part[1:-1]
                    if 'a similar argument exists' in line:
                        parts[pi]="'"+G(inner)+"'"
                    else:
                        parts[pi]="'"+(Y(inner) if qcount==0 else G(inner))+"'"
                    qcount+=1
            out.append(''.join(parts)); continue
        if '[possible values:' in line:
            def _pv(m):
                vals=[G(v.strip()) for v in m.group(1).split(',')]
                return '[possible values: '+', '.join(vals)+']'
            line=re.sub(r'\[possible values: ([^\]]+)\]',_pv,line)
            out.append(line); continue
        if line.startswith('Usage:') or (line.startswith('       ') and (line.lstrip().startswith(prog+' ') or line.lstrip().startswith(prog+'\t'))):
            if line.startswith('Usage:'):
                line='\x1b[1m\x1b[4mUsage:\x1b[0m'+line[len('Usage:'):]
            # bold prog (+ cache as one unit if present)
            # find prog occurrence
            pos=line.find(prog)
            if pos!=-1:
                end=pos+len(prog)
                if line[end:end+6]==' cache':
                    line=line[:pos]+B(line[pos:end+6])+line[end+6:]
                else:
                    line=line[:pos]+B(prog)+line[end:]
            # bold long option names in usage (name only, not ... or placeholder)
            line=re.sub(r'(?<![\w-])(--[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)(?=\.\.\.|\s|<|$)',lambda mm:B(mm.group(1)),line)
            out.append(line); continue
        if line.strip()=='--build':
            out.append('  '+G('--build')); continue
        if line.startswith("For more information, try '--help'."):
            line=line.replace("'--help'","'"+B('--help')+"'")
            out.append(line); continue
        out.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(out)
'''

s=s.replace("if sys.stderr.isatty() and os.environ.get('TERM') not in (None,'','dumb') and not (os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')):", "if sys.stderr.isatty() and os.environ.get('TERM') not in (None,'','dumb') and not os.environ.get('NO_COLOR') and os.environ.get('CLICOLOR')!='0':")
p.write_text(s)

def do_help(r, kind):
    text=(HELP_LONG if kind=='long' else HELP_SHORT).decode()
    try:
        _hw=os.get_terminal_size(1).columns if sys.stdout.isatty() else 100
    except Exception:
        _hw=100
    text=rewrap_help(text, min(100,_hw) if _hw else 100)
    def gen(w):
        if r.colored:
            w.write(highlight_text_block(text,'Command Help',r,force_truecolor=True))
        else:
            w.write(text.encode())
    output_via_pager(r,['STDIN'],gen)
    return 0

def do_list_languages(r):
    langs=languages_for_listing()
    def gen(w):
        if not r.colored:
            for name,exts in langs:
                w.write(f"{name}:{','.join(exts)}\n")
        else:
            w.write(format_languages_colored(langs,r.term_width))
    output_via_pager(r,['STDIN'],gen)
    return 0

def format_languages_colored(langs,term_width):
    maxlen=max(len(n) for n,_ in langs)
    col=maxlen+1
    limit=term_width-maxlen-2
    out=[]
    def ge(e): return f"\x1b[32m\x1b[32m{e}\x1b[0m"
    for name,exts in langs:
        lines=[]; cur=[]; curw=0; first=True
        for e in exts:
            w=len(e)+2
            if cur and curw+w>limit:
                lines.append(cur); cur=[e]; curw=w; first=False; continue
            if not cur and first and w>limit:
                # name on its own line, ext on next (overflow allowed on its own line)
                lines.append([]); cur=[e]; curw=w; first=False; continue
            cur.append(e); curw+=w
        lines.append(cur)
        for idx,line_exts in enumerate(lines):
            prefix=name.ljust(col) if idx==0 else ' '*col
            styled=', '.join(ge(p) for p in line_exts)
            if idx < len(lines)-1 and line_exts: styled+=', '
            out.append(prefix+styled+'\n')
    return ''.join(out).encode()
